sources.title: AgentAbstain: Do LLM Agents Know When Not to Act?

inspection_spans.observation: Agentic abstention is framed as a sequential act-or-abstain decision before a potentially irreversible commit; the benchmark has 263 paired tasks and 42 executable sandboxes.
The taxonomy distinguishes successful or implicit abstention, no abstention, and post-hoc abstention after an irreversible action.
The evaluation is deterministic, single-agent and single-turn; multilingual evaluation is explicitly left to future work.

sources.supports: A commit-boundary, trace-observable construct for agentic abstention.
sources.does_not_establish: Any multilingual effect, a language-conditioned authorization failure, or deployment prevalence.

sources.title: All Languages Matter: On the Multilingual Safety of LLMs

inspection_spans.observation: A monolingual safety set is translated and professionally checked across ten languages, fourteen safety issues, and text-response attacks.
Automatic self-evaluation is inaccurate and the tested mitigation is insufficient.

sources.supports: Language-conditioned variation in unsafe text responses under a multilingual content-safety benchmark.
sources.does_not_establish: Tool authorization, irreversible action commits, or act-versus-abstain traces.

controller_boundary: Inspection repairs source identity and locator gaps only. It does not promote the program, establish a research gap, or represent these files as Zotero attachments.
